questions.q: Which amine can be prepared by the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
questions.explain: Benzyl chloride undergoes SN2 with the phthalimide anion, so benzylamine is obtained. Aryl and tertiary halides do not undergo SN2, and secondary amines are never products.

questions.q: Why is the N–H hydrogen of phthalimide acidic enough to be removed by ethanolic KOH?
options: Potassium forms a covalent bond with nitrogen
The benzene ring withdraws electrons directly from nitrogen by induction only
The negative charge of the anion is delocalised onto two flanking C=O groups
questions.explain: Nitrogen sits between two carbonyl groups, so the imide anion is stabilised by resonance onto both oxygens. This is what makes potassium phthalimide easy to form.

questions.q: In the Ing–Manske modification, the N-alkylphthalimide is cleaved with:
options: Hydrazine, giving phthalhydrazide as a precipitate
questions.explain: Hydrazine releases the primary amine under milder conditions and phthalhydrazide precipitates. Alkaline hydrolysis is the NCERT version, not the Ing–Manske one.

questions.q: Only primary amines are obtained in the Gabriel synthesis, with no secondary or tertiary amines. The reason is that:
options: alkyl halides react only once with any nitrogen nucleophile
the N-alkylphthalimide has no N–H left and cannot be alkylated again
the hydrolysis step destroys secondary amines
KOH removes any secondary amine as its salt
questions.explain: After one alkylation the nitrogen carries no H, so over-alkylation, the main problem in ammonolysis of alkyl halides, cannot happen.
